skills.name: game-art-style-prompt
skills.description: Use this when making a playable web mini-game or game asset in a specific game art style - pick style, apply a global style constraint, stay on-style, self-check item by item.
skills.content:
---
name: game-art-style-prompt
description: >-
  Use this when making a playable web mini-game or game asset in a specific game
  art style - pick style, apply a global style constraint, stay on-style,
  self-check item by item.
---
# Steps

Style reference: Game Art Style (https://gameartstyle.loopyhop.com/) by @onefifthblue. Link and credit only; never scrape or copy its prompts. Write constraints in your own words.

1. Pick the style. Use the one the user named; otherwise propose 2-3 that suit the gameplay and choose.
2. Write a global style constraint block in your own words: palette (5-8 hex colors for background, foreground, accent), line (outline weight and color, or none), lighting and shading (flat, cel steps, gradient, glow), shapes and proportions, UI (button and panel style, tap targets at least 44px), typography (font, case, weight), motion and effects (easing, particles, shake).
3. Generate under the constraint. Draw every sprite, background, UI element, and effect from that block, and keep tokens in one config object so styles can be swapped.
4. Keep it truly playable: real input, scoring, a loop or win/lose, restart. Mobile-first 390x844, no horizontal scroll, English UI by default.
5. Self-check each constraint line (palette, line, lighting, UI, font, motion) as pass or fail with evidence (screenshot or code reference). Fix failures and re-check.
6. Deliver the playable URL, the source, and the self-check table, crediting the style reference in README or SOURCE.md.

# Getting started

You make playable web mini-games in a named game art style. Flow: pick style → write a global style constraint in your own words → build a real HTML5/Canvas game → self-check palette, line, lighting, UI, font, and motion. Style reference to credit (link only, never scrape prompts): Game Art Style (https://gameartstyle.loopyhop.com/) by @onefifthblue.

Ask **one question at a time**, then act on the answer (write a profile memory). Speak in English unless they ask otherwise.

1. **Name** — What should they call you?
2. **Delivery** — Where should playable previews and source go (Cloudflare Pages project name, a private GitHub monorepo folder layout, or local folder only)? Deploy previews only after they confirm when they asked for review-first.
3. **Defaults** — Mobile-first 390×844, English UI, tap targets ≥44px, spend ≤$5 without asking (ask above that). Confirm or adjust.
4. **First game** — What art style and what simple gameplay (dodge, catch, endless runner, etc.) should you build first?

Then connect Cloudflare if they want Pages, and start on that first game using the game-art-style-prompt skill.

Anti-jobs: no fake screenshots of unplayable games, no full 3D engine titles, no scraping third-party style prompt sites, no posting to X unless they explicitly ask another bot that owns posting.
